$comment: Every text a developer reads from the SDKs and the ncdb command line, in one place (NOC-329). Each entry: its id (<kind>.<name>), its kind (notice, error, part of an error's message, or cli, a text of the command line), for a notice or an error its code as RFC 0009 spells it (an error returned with several codes names each, separated by ' | '), the text, with {name} or {name:?} where a value goes, and when it shows. Entries are sorted by id, one field per line, so `git diff` shows each change readably; `pnpm texts` lists what changed since the last release for the owner's review. scripts/texts.mjs generates crates/nocentraldb/src/texts/ and crates/ncdb/src/texts.rs from this file and checks it in the gates; run `node scripts/texts.mjs --write` after an edit.

texts.text: additive: clients on model version {from} keep every change written under version {to}.
texts.when: `ncdb model build`, the last line of a new model version's report: the change is additive.

texts.text: cannot be opened: {error}
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when its path cannot be resolved; `error` is the system's reason.

texts.text: cannot be read: {error}
texts.when: After the lock's name, when the lock cannot be read from disk, or is no lock JSON; `error` is the system's or the core's reason.

texts.text: cannot be written: {error}
texts.when: After the lock's name, from `ncdb model build`, when the lock cannot be written; `error` is the system's reason.

texts.text: the SDK described the model in a form this ncdb cannot read: {error}
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when the SDK's description of the model is no JSON this `ncdb` reads, as when the SDK and `ncdb` are of different releases; `error` is the core's reason.

texts.text: descriptions changed (model version stays {version})
texts.when: `ncdb model build`, after the lock's name, when only descriptions changed, so the model version stays; a line per change follows.

texts.text: its model.hash does not match its content, so it was edited by hand. Restore it from version control, and change the schema instead.
texts.when: After the lock's name, when the lock's `model.hash` does not match its content.

texts.text: {lock}: missing; run ncdb model build.
texts.when: `ncdb model check` when there is no lock at `--lock`.

texts.text: model needs a command: build or check
texts.when: `ncdb model` with nothing after it; the usage follows.

texts.text: model version 1, a new model ({id})
texts.when: `ncdb model build`, after the lock's name, when it wrote the first lock of a model; `id` is the new model id. A line per collection follows.

texts.text: no command
texts.when: `ncdb` run with no arguments; the usage follows.

texts.text: no such file; the schema module is ./model.ts unless --model names another.
texts.when: After the schema module's name, from `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check`, when there is no file at `--model`.

texts.text: ncdb runs the schema with Node.js {major} or later, and found no `node` on PATH.
texts.when: After the schema module's name, from `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check`, when no `node` is on PATH.

texts.text: cannot start Node.js: {error}
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when `node` is on PATH but cannot be started; `error` is the system's reason.

texts.text: ncdb runs the schema with Node.js {major} or later, and the `node` on PATH is {version}.
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when the `node` on PATH is older than Node.js 24, or does not say its version; `version` is its version, or `cli.nodeVersionUnknown`.

texts.text: of an unknown version
texts.when: The `version` of `cli.nodeTooOld` when `node --version` printed nothing.

texts.text: {option} needs a path
texts.when: `--model` or `--lock` given last, or followed by another option; the usage follows.

texts.text: {lock}: out of date; run ncdb model build. It would write {would}
texts.when: `ncdb model check` when the lock differs from what `ncdb model build` would write; `would` is what build would report, or `cli.rewriteCanonical`.

texts.text: {lock}: refused, the model breaks the rules (no lock is written)
texts.when: `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check` when the core refuses a first model; each refusal follows on a line of its own.

texts.text: {lock}: refused, the change is not additive (model version stays {version})
texts.when: `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check` when the core refuses the change against the previous lock; each refusal follows on a line of its own.

texts.text: rewrite it in its canonical form (model version stays {version})
texts.when: After `cli.outOfDate`, from `ncdb model check`, when the lock describes the model but is not written in its canonical form, so `build` would only rewrite it.

texts.text: cannot be run: {error}
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when Node.js cannot import it; `error` is the exception's message.

texts.text: exports no model; export the model as `export const model = nc.model(...)`.
texts.when: After the schema module's name, when the module imports but exports no `model` made with `nc.model`.

texts.text: unknown command: {command}
texts.when: `ncdb` run with a first word other than `model` or `help`; the usage follows.

texts.text: unknown command: model {command}
texts.when: `ncdb model` followed by a word other than `build` or `check`; the usage follows.

texts.text: unknown option: {option}
texts.when: `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check` given an option other than `--model` or `--lock`; the usage follows.

texts.text: {lock}: up to date (model version {version})
texts.when: `ncdb model build` and `ncdb model check` when the lock already says what the schema says, byte for byte.

texts.text:
usage: ncdb model build [--model <path>] [--lock <path>]
       ncdb model check [--model <path>] [--lock <path>]

build reads the schema module (--model, default ./model.ts, which exports
`model`) and the previous lock (--lock, default ./model.lock.json), refuses a
change that clients on the previous model could not keep, and writes the lock.
check does the same and writes nothing: it fails when the lock is missing or
out of date, or the change is refused. Both run the schema with Node.js 24 or
later, found on PATH.
texts.when: `ncdb --help`, `ncdb -h` or `ncdb help` prints it; after a usage error, `ncdb` prints it below the error.

texts.text: model version {from} -> {to}
texts.when: `ncdb model build`, after the lock's name, when it wrote a new model version; a line per change follows, then `cli.additive`.

texts.text: collection
texts.when: In core.refusalBadName and core.refusalNameClash, as `kind` or `other_kind`, for the name of a collection.

texts.text: computed field
texts.when: In core.refusalBadName and core.refusalNameClash, as `kind` or `other_kind`, for the name of a computed field.

texts.text: field
texts.when: In core.refusalBadName and core.refusalNameClash, as `kind` or `other_kind`, for the name of a field.

texts.text: index
texts.when: In core.refusalBadName and core.refusalNameClash, as `kind` or `other_kind`, for the name of an index.

texts.text: view
texts.when: In core.refusalBadName and core.refusalNameClash, as `kind` or `other_kind`, for the name of a view.

texts.text:
{kind} {name}: the name breaks the naming rules.
A name starts with a lower-case letter and has at most 63 ASCII letters and digits.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a name breaks the naming rules. `kind` is a core.nameKind text; `name` is the name, after its collection's for a name in a collection.

texts.text:
collection {collection}: removed. Changes name collections; data in {collection} would belong to nothing.
To stop using it, keep it in the schema. To rename it, add the collection under its new name.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a collection of the previous lock is missing from the next one.

texts.text:
collection {collection}: no longer deprecated.
Clients that stopped writing it would not write it again.
Keep it deprecated, and add a new collection instead.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a deprecated collection is no longer deprecated.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: the config of {type_id} changes.
The config is part of the type's merge rule: members would merge existing values differently.
Add a new field with the new config instead, and deprecate {collection}.{field}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a plugin field's config changes, appears or disappears.

texts.text: {collection}.{field}: option {option} is listed twice.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a choice lists an option twice.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: removed. Changes name fields; data in {collection}.{field} would belong to nothing.
To stop using it, keep it in the schema with .deprecated("..."). To rename it, add {rename}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a field of the previous lock is missing from the next one. `rename` is the one new field of the same type in the collection, when there is exactly one, else core.refusalNoRename.

texts.text:
index {collection}.{index}: equal is {equal}, but the index has {fields} fields.
No query could fix more fields than the index has.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: an index's equal is larger than its number of fields.

texts.text:
index {collection}.{index}: {collection}.{field} is {type_id}, which cannot be indexed.
An index can use basic values and single links (nc.link).
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: an index names a field of a type that cannot be indexed.

texts.text: index {collection}.{index}: {collection} has no field {field}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: an index names a field its collection does not have.

texts.text:
model.version: {next} is lower than {previous}.
The lock is older than the previous one; it is not its successor.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: the next lock's model version is lower than the previous one's.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: marked personal.
Its earlier values are in the log under the space key only; erasing a person would not reach them.
Add a new personal field instead, and deprecate {collection}.{field}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: an existing field is marked personal.

texts.text:
{kind} {name}: the name collides with the {other_kind} {other}.
Names in one scope must differ in more than case: the local view is SQLite, whose column names ignore case.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: two names in one scope are equal, or differ only in case. `kind` and `other_kind` are core.nameKind texts.

texts.text: a field under the new name
texts.when: In core.refusalFieldRemoved, as `rename`, when the collection has no one new field of the removed field's type.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: options change from [{from}] to [{to}].
Stored values name options, and their order may become sort order.
Keep every option where it is, and append new options at the end.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a choice's options are not the previous ones with new ones appended. `from` and `to` are the options, separated by commas.

texts.text:
model.id: {next} is not {previous}.
The lock belongs to another model; it is not a successor of the previous one.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: the next lock is of another lineage. `next` and `previous` are the model ids.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: its person changes from {from} to {to}.
Old values stay sealed under the keys of the old person: the field would be half erasable.
Keep .personal({{ person: "{from}" }}), or add a new personal field.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a personal field's person changes.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: personal to {collection}.{person}, which is itself personal.
The link that names the person must stay readable, so the SDK can find the person's key.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a personal field's person is a link field that is itself personal.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: personal to {person}, which is no link field of {collection}.
person is "self" or the name of an nc.link field of {collection}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a personal field's person is no link field of its collection.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: {type_id} cannot be personal.
Only basic values can be personal: nc.string, nc.int, nc.float, nc.boolean and nc.oneOf.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a field of a type that cannot be personal is marked personal.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: the rule version of {type_id} changes from {from} to {to}.
A new rule version needs a migration that every member runs first, and there is none yet.
Add a new field with rule version {to} instead, and deprecate {collection}.{field}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a field moves to another rule version of its type.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: target {target} removed.
Existing links into {target} would read as wrong collection, and references into it as missing, on upgraded clients only.
Keep {target} in the targets.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a collection is removed from the targets of a link or a reference.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: type changes from {from} to {to}.
Clients would merge and read existing values differently.
Add a new field instead, and deprecate {collection}.{field}.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a field's type changes (for a set, its element's type).

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: no longer deprecated.
Clients that stopped writing it would not write it again.
Keep it deprecated, and add a new field instead.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a deprecated field is no longer deprecated.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: {type_id} names no plugin of the model.
A plugin's field type needs its namespace in plugins.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a plugin field type's namespace is not in the model's plugins.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: {type_id} has no rule version {rule}.
This version knows rule version {known} of every built-in type.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a built-in field type names a rule version this core does not know. `known` is the one it knows.

texts.text: {collection}.{field}: target {target} is no collection of the model.
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses a model that breaks a rule on its own, and in the error of opening with such a lock: a link's target is no collection of the model.

texts.text:
{collection}.{field}: no longer personal.
Old values stay sealed under person keys and new ones would not be: the field would be half erasable.
Keep .personal({{ person: "{person}" }}).
texts.when: Under the lock's name, when `ncdb model build` or `ncdb model check` refuses the change against the previous lock, and in the error of opening with a lock the database refuses against the one it was last opened with: a personal field is no longer personal.

texts.text: the account key cannot be sealed to the invitation's member
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) when the account key cannot be sealed to the invitation's member key.

texts.text: the account space already records an account key with this number
texts.when: Renewing the account key, on removing a lost member, when the account space already records an account key with the next number.

texts.text: a local ad-hoc space is not built yet; create a synced one
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) with `local`: local ad-hoc spaces wait for a ticket of their own (Carsten, 2026-11-15, NOC-320 Q3).

texts.text: personal fields are not copied into an ad-hoc space yet, until an erasure reaches the copy
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) with `personal`: copies of personal fields wait until an erasure reaches a copy in another space (Carsten, 2026-11-15, NOC-320 Q8).

texts.text: the object {id} is deleted, and a deleted object is not copied
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) when an object to copy is deleted (Carsten, 2026-11-15, NOC-320 Q7).

texts.text: the space {space} holds no object {id} to copy
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) when this database holds no such object in that space.

texts.text: the object {id} is named twice, and an ad-hoc space holds one copy of it
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) when the objects to copy name the same object twice.

texts.text: the invitation's agent already has an account: linking an agent is not built yet
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) with the invitation of an agent that already has an account.

texts.text: the invitation's member is a device of this account already
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) with the invitation of a device of this account already.

texts.text: the invitation's member is a member of the space already
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) when the invitation's member is a member of the space already.

texts.text: members.add takes at least one invitation
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: members.add with an empty list of invitations.

texts.text: members.add takes invitations
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: members.add without its invitations.

texts.text: after is a cursor
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: find given an after that is not a cursor.

texts.text: {key} is text
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a request whose argument, such as space or lock, is missing or not text.

texts.text: a device joins with a role
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: members.add of a device without a role.

texts.text: equal is an array
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: find given equal values that are not an array.

texts.text: a field's name is text
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write whose values name a field by something that is not text.

texts.text: find takes a query
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: find (db.find, space.find) without its query.

texts.text: an invitation is text
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: members.add given an invitation that is not text.

texts.text: a kind is "device" or "agent"
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: account.pair (db.account.pair) given a kind that is neither.

texts.text: no call {call}
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a request whose call the bridge does not have.

texts.text: no op {op}
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write op the bridge does not have.

texts.text: change is not a change id
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: sync.isConfirmed (db.sync.isConfirmed) given a change that is not a change id.

texts.text: not a value a field takes
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write of a value no field type takes.

texts.text: a member id is 64 lowercase hex digits
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a membership or account call given a member id that is not 64 lowercase hex digits.

texts.text: a request is a map of id, call and args
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a request that is not a map with a positive id, a call and its args.

texts.text: a role is reader, writer or admin
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a membership call given a role that is none of them.

texts.text: not a space id
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a call given a space that is not a space id.

texts.text: a map value is $add or $remove with a list
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write of a map value that is not nc.add(...) or nc.remove(...).

texts.text: not an object id
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a call given an object id that is not one.

texts.text: too large
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write of an integer above the largest a field holds.

texts.text: too small
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write of an integer below the smallest a field holds.

texts.text: the database is open already
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: open, on a worker whose database is open.

texts.text: open takes inMemory: true, or a name in the browser
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: open (nc.open) given neither.

texts.text: a role is text
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: members.add or members.setRole given a role that is not text.

texts.text: take is a number
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: find given a take that is not a number.

texts.text: values is a map
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: a write op whose values are not a map.

texts.text: a write takes ops
texts.when: The bridge, on a request from the TypeScript SDK: write (space.write and its shorthands) without its ops.

texts.text: the invitation's certificate does not hold
texts.when: Members::add and Account::pair (members.add, db.account.pair) when the invitation's certificate does not verify, or certifies another member.

texts.text: the invitation's certificate is under an account key its account replaced
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) when the invitation's certificate is under an account key its account has since replaced.

texts.text: the cursor belongs to another model, index or equality prefix
texts.when: A query continued with a cursor of another model, index or equality prefix.

texts.text: the database cannot be opened: another tab holds it, or {error}
texts.when: nc.open in a browser, when OPFS refuses the database: most often another tab holds it; the reason follows.

texts.text: a database name is 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, - and _
texts.when: nc.open in a browser, when the database name is empty, longer than 64 characters or has another character than a-z, 0-9, - and _.

texts.text: a device does not remove itself as lost
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) when the member to remove is this device.

texts.text: the query does not give one value per field of the index's equality prefix
texts.when: A query that does not give one value per field of the index's equality prefix.

texts.text: the erasure request is another member's
texts.when: Db::erase with a request another member made: only its performer erases with it (NOC-325).

texts.text: the field does not hold {asked}
texts.when: Object::get::<T> when the field holds another kind of value than T.

texts.text: the database was folded by another model than the lock's, and holds no lock to check this one against
texts.when: Opening, when the database holds a view of another model and no lock to check the new one against.

texts.text: an index row has no object
texts.when: A query whose index names an object the view does not hold: the view is damaged.

texts.text: an index that runs in one space is read with space.find, any other with db.find
texts.when: A query of a space-scoped index with db.find, or of any other index with space.find.

texts.text: IndexedDB holds only one of the database's two key records; new keys would open none of its spaces
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when IndexedDB holds only one of the database's two key records, the wrapping key or the wrapped keys.

texts.text: the database exists, but IndexedDB holds no keys for it; new keys would open none of its spaces
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when the database exists on OPFS but IndexedDB holds no keys for it.

texts.text: {what}: {name}{hint}
texts.when: nc.open in a browser, when IndexedDB refuses to open, read, write or use the member's keys: what failed, the browser's error name and a hint.

texts.text: the invitation's member waits to be paired and has no certificate yet
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) with the invitation of a database waiting to be paired, which has no certificate yet.

texts.text: {what}: {error}
texts.when: Opening, when the file system fails on the database's directory, file or key file: what failed, then the system's error, never the path.

texts.text: the key file holds no keys of this SDK's format
texts.when: Opening with a key file (OpenOptions::key_file) whose content is not keys of this SDK's format.

texts.text: the database exists, but its key file does not; new keys would open none of its spaces
texts.when: Opening a database at a path with a key file (OpenOptions::key_file) when the database exists but the key file does not.

texts.text: the key record of the database does not open under its wrapping key
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when the database's key record does not open under its wrapping key.

texts.text: the key record of the database holds no keys of this SDK's format
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when the database's key record holds no keys of this SDK's format.

texts.text: the keystore entry of the database holds no keys of this SDK's format
texts.when: Opening a database at a path when its platform keystore entry holds no keys of this SDK's format.

texts.text: the keystore entry of the database cannot be read
texts.when: Opening a database at a path when its platform keystore entry cannot be read.

texts.text: the keystore failed: {error}
texts.when: Opening a database at a path when the platform keystore fails; its error follows.

texts.text: the database exists, but the keystore holds no keys for it; new keys would open none of its spaces
texts.when: Opening a database at a path when it exists but the platform keystore holds no keys for it.

texts.text: no platform keystore is reachable ({why}); name a key file with key_file(path)
texts.when: Opening a database at a path when no platform keystore is reachable, as on a headless Linux without the Secret Service; a key file (OpenOptions::key_file) is the way out.

texts.text: the space's last admin may not leave it
texts.when: Space::leave (space.leave) when this member is the space's last admin.

texts.text: the space's last admin may not lower its own role
texts.when: Members::set_role (members.setRole) when the space's last admin lowers its own role.

texts.text: the lock is refused: {invalid:?}
texts.when: Opening, when the lock breaks the rules RFC 0005 gives a lock; the core's finding follows.

texts.text: the lock is refused: {error}
texts.when: Opening, when the lock cannot be read; the reason follows.

texts.text: a member does not remove itself: leaving a space is space.leave()
texts.when: Members::remove (members.remove) when the member to remove is this member: leaving is Space::leave.

texts.text: the account space already records a newer account key, which this device has not taken yet
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) while the account space records an account key newer than this device's own: the device takes it when it syncs.

texts.text: this database holds no account key; a device of the account signs off
texts.when: Account::sign_off on a database that holds no account key, an agent's or one waiting to be paired (NOC-325).

texts.text: the device holds no account space
texts.when: Renewing the account key, on removing a lost member, on a device that holds no account space.

texts.text: this browser context has no IndexedDB, which keeps the member's keys
texts.when: nc.open in a browser context without IndexedDB, where the member's keys live.

texts.text: the member is no longer a member of the space
texts.when: A membership call or a write by a member that was removed from the space, or that the relay answered not_member or removed_member for.

texts.text: the field {name} of {collection} has the plugin type {type_id}, rule {rule}, which no plugin given to OpenOptions::plugin implements
texts.when: A write to a plugin field whose plugin type no plugin given to OpenOptions::plugin implements.

texts.text: the account space records no such member of the account
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) when the account space records no member of the account with that id.

texts.text: the model has no collection {collection}
texts.when: A read or a write that names a collection the model does not have.

texts.text: the collection {collection} has no field {name}
texts.when: A write that names a field the collection does not have.

texts.text: the object's collection has no field {name}
texts.when: Object::get when the object's collection has no field of that name.

texts.text: the model declares no index {name} of {collection}
texts.when: Db::index (db.index) when the model declares no index of that name on the collection.

texts.text: the model declares no such index
texts.when: A query of an index the model does not declare.

texts.text: the copy holds no object {object} in {collection}
texts.when: An update, a delete or a restore of an object this copy does not hold in that collection.

texts.text: the copy holds no space {space}
texts.when: A call that names a space this database holds no copy of: Space::erasures, Members::list, and every write or read of a space.

texts.text: this browser context has no WebCrypto, which keeps the member's keys
texts.when: nc.open in a browser context without WebCrypto, which wraps the member's keys.

texts.text: IndexedDB holds no wrapping key for the database
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when the database's key record exists but its wrapping key is gone from IndexedDB.

texts.text: the member is not a member of the space
texts.when: Members::remove and Members::set_role (members.remove, members.setRole) when the member id is not a current member of the space.

texts.text: the text is not a pairing answer: {why}
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) when the text is not a pairing answer; the core's reason follows.

texts.text: the words are no recovery code
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) when the words it was given are no recovery code.

texts.text: the text is not an erasure request: {why}
texts.when: Parsing an erasure request from text (ErasureRequest::from_str) when the text is not one; the reason follows (NOC-325).

texts.text: not {name} in {len} lowercase hex digits
texts.when: Parsing an id from text (SpaceId, ObjectId, ChangeId, MemberId) when the text is not that many lowercase hex digits.

texts.text: the text is not an invitation: {why}
texts.when: Parsing an invitation from text (Invitation::from_str; nc.invitation) when the text is not one; the reason follows.

texts.text: the text is not a set of sign-offs: {why}
texts.when: Parsing sign-offs from text (SignOffs::from_str) when the text is not one; the reason follows (NOC-325).

texts.text: this database is not waiting to be paired
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) on a database not opened for pairing.

texts.text: the object is no person's: it has no personal field
texts.when: Db::erasure_request with an object that has no personal field, so it names no person to erase (NOC-325).

texts.text: only an agent adds a sub-agent: it signs the sub-agent's certificate with its own member key
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) with a sub-agent's invitation, version 3, on a device's or a sub-agent's database: only an agent signs a sub-agent's certificate (NOC-320 Q2).

texts.text: a database at a name opens only in a dedicated Web Worker
texts.when: nc.open in a browser, when a database at a name is opened outside a dedicated Web Worker, where OPFS cannot be used.

texts.text: the options name a browser database together with a path, a key file or in_memory(); name one place
texts.when: Opening with options that name a browser database together with a path, a key file or in_memory().

texts.text: the options name both a key file and in_memory(); keys in memory need no file
texts.when: Opening with options that name both a key file and in_memory().

texts.text: the options name no place for the database: call path(dir) or in_memory()
texts.when: Opening with options that name no place: neither a path, nor in_memory(), nor a browser name.

texts.text: the options name both a path and in_memory(); name one
texts.when: Opening with options that name both a path and in_memory().

texts.text: the options name sub_agent() together with agent(), pairing() or recover(); a sub-agent is none of them
texts.when: Opening with OpenOptions::sub_agent together with agent(), pairing() or recover().

texts.text: the page size is 0 or above 1000
texts.when: A query whose page size is 0 or above 1000.

texts.text: this database holds no account key, so it pairs nobody
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) on a database that holds no account key.

texts.text: the invitation asks to be paired as the other kind
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) when the kind it is given differs from the kind the invitation asks to be paired as.

texts.text: the pairing answer does not hold for this database: {why}
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) when the answer is not for this database or does not verify; the core's reason follows.

texts.text: a database waiting to be paired creates no space until its pairing completes
texts.when: Spaces::create (db.spaces.create) on a database waiting to be paired.

texts.text: the person's key is not held on this device yet
texts.when: A write of a personal field whose person's key this device does not hold yet: it holds it once it fetched the key's record.

texts.text: the person link {link} of {collection} is unset
texts.when: A write of a personal field whose person link is unset, so the SDK cannot tell whose data it is.

texts.text: the database holds an unreadable plugin state
texts.when: A write to a plugin's field whose stored state the plugin cannot read.

texts.text: the recovery code is not this account's
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) when the recovery code given is of another account.

texts.text: the words are not a recovery code: {why}
texts.when: Opening with a recovery code (OpenOptions::recover; nc.open with recover) when the words are not a recovery code; the reason names a word's position, never the word.

texts.text: the database exists: a recovery code recovers the account onto a new one
texts.when: Opening with a recovery code when the database exists: a recovery code recovers the account onto a new database only.

texts.text: the relay no longer serves this member the space {id}
texts.when: A write to a space the relay no longer serves this member: it was removed.

texts.text: the relay URL must start with wss:// or ws://
texts.when: Opening, when the relay URL starts with neither wss:// nor ws://.

texts.text: only a device that holds the account key removes a member of the account
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) on a database that holds no account key: only a device of the account removes a member of it.

texts.text: only {role} of the space {doing}
texts.when: A membership call or a write by a member whose role does not allow it: which role is needed, and for what.

texts.text: the member holds no key of a generation the rotation must chain; it rotates once an envelope for it arrives
texts.when: A removal, or an add after a rotation, when this member lacks a key generation the rotation must chain; it works once an envelope for it arrives.

texts.text: the member does not hold a person key of the space, which the rotation must re-wrap; it rotates once it fetched the key's record
texts.when: A removal, or an add after a rotation, when this member lacks a person key of the space that the rotation must re-wrap; it works once it fetched the key's record.

texts.text: a sign-off does not hold for this erasure in its space; nothing was erased
texts.when: Db::erase when one of the sign-offs would not hold in its space by RFC 0008's rules; it writes no shred in any space (NOC-325).

texts.text: the space's clock: {error}
texts.when: A write, when the space's clock cannot be read or written; the error follows.

texts.text: the space {id} is of the model {space_model}, the lock is of the model {lock_model}
texts.when: A write to, or a read of, a space whose model is not the lock's.

texts.text: the account key statement does not verify
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) when the account key statement the invitation carries does not verify.

texts.text: the statement's number is too high
texts.when: Renewing the account key, on removing a lost member, when the account key statement's number cannot grow further.

texts.text: a sub-agent creates no space: its parent adds it to the spaces it works in
texts.when: Spaces::create (db.spaces.create) on a sub-agent's database (OpenOptions::sub_agent): it works in the spaces its parent adds it to.

texts.text: a sub-agent is not paired into an account: its parent agent adds it to the spaces it works in
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) with a sub-agent's invitation, version 3 (NOC-320 Q1).

texts.text: only an admin of the performer's account takes an erasure back
texts.when: Erasures::take_back by a member that is not an admin of the account that performed the erasure (NOC-325).

texts.text: the shred is no provisional erasure of this space that is still pending
texts.when: Erasures::take_back with a shred that is final, already finalized or taken back, or not of the space (NOC-325).

texts.text: the invitation's account is new to this database: pass its fingerprint once a person compared it
texts.when: Members::add (members.add) without a fingerprint when the invitation's account is new to this database; the error carries the fingerprint a person compares.

texts.text: the value does not fit the field {field} of {collection}
texts.when: A write whose value is not of the field's type.

texts.text: the value does not fit the field {field} of {collection}: {why}
texts.when: A write to a plugin's field whose plugin refuses the value; the plugin's reason follows.

texts.text: the local view failed: {error}
texts.when: Any call, when the local view's SQLite fails: storageFull when the disk or the quota is full, storageFailed otherwise; the core's error follows.

texts.text: {what}: {name}
texts.when: nc.open in a browser when WebCrypto fails to make the wrapping key or to seal the key record: what failed, and the name of the error it threw, never a byte.

texts.text: Your account has a new account key. Members that have not learnt it yet still accept the old one.
texts.when: Account::remove_member (db.account.removeMember) returns it once a lost member is removed and the account key renewed. The owner's text, NOC-273.

texts.text: Spaces this database joined before keep its old account. Other members see it as linked to yours.
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) returns it besides devicePaired or agentPaired when the database had joined spaces under an account of its own, now linked into the one it paired with. The owner's text, NOC-273.

texts.text: Your account is back with a new account key. Your spaces come back when one of their members adds this device.
texts.when: db.account().recovered() gives it on the open that recovered the account from its code (OpenOptions::recover; nc.open with recover), with a new account key on this device. The owner's text, NOC-273; NOC-289.

texts.text: This space limits what the sub-agent can decrypt, not what a process running as the same user can read. Its copies keep no link to an object that was not copied, and no personal or plugin field.
texts.when: Spaces::create_ad_hoc (db.spaces.createAdHoc) returns it once the ad-hoc space and its copies are written. The first sentence is the owner's, NOC-320 Q10; how many links and plugin fields were left out, the call returns beside it.

texts.text: This agent acts for your account in the spaces an admin adds it to. It holds no account key.
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) returns it on an agent once its account certified it. The owner's text, NOC-273.

texts.text: Your new device was added to this space and reads its whole history.
texts.when: Account::pair (db.account.pair) returns it once per space it added the new device to. The owner's text, NOC-273.

texts.text: This device now holds your account key. Keep your recovery code: it is the way back if you lose every device.
texts.when: Account::complete_pairing (db.account.completePairing) returns it on a device once it holds the account key. The owner's text, NOC-273.

texts.text: The person's personal fields are erased in these spaces. Devices that never come back online, copies made outside the database and unmarked free text keep them; other devices and agents of this account erase only when they run the erasure too.
texts.when: Db::erase returns it with the shreds it wrote, once per call, in every space of the database where a sign-off came for the person's keys. Carsten, 2026-11-15, NOC-326 (Q6).

texts.text: Personal data was erased on a device of this account. The erasure becomes final after 7 days; until then an admin of this account can take it back.
texts.when: No call returns it: the space status gives it with each provisional erasure (provisional_erasures, provisionalErasures), on every device of the account, while an erasure in a space with one account waits out its 7 days. pm's text, NOC-234.

texts.text: The new member reads the whole history of this space.
texts.when: Members::add (members.add in TypeScript) returns it once the member is added to the space: the new member reads every change written before it joined.

texts.text: The removed member keeps its copy of everything it received before now.
texts.when: Members::remove (members.remove) returns it once a member is removed and the space key rotated: the removed member keeps what it already received. RFC 0009's text.

texts.text: A member whose role was lowered keeps its copy of everything it received before now.
texts.when: Members::set_role (members.setRole) returns it on every role change, raised or lowered: a lowered member keeps what it received. The owner's text, NOC-203.

texts.text: This member keeps its copy of everything it received before now. Until an admin rotates the space key, the others write under a key it still holds.
texts.when: Space::leave (space.leave) returns it once this member's removal of itself is written: it keeps its copy, and the space key changes only when an admin rotates. The owner's text, NOC-219.

texts.text: The erasure is taken back in this space, and the person's fields read again; a finalize another device of the account wrote before it saw this take-back still wins, and the person stays erased.
texts.when: space.erasures().take_back(shred) returns it once an admin of the performer's account took a provisional erasure back within its 7 days. pm, NOC-326, on the coding agent's proposal (Q7).

texts.text: the database directory cannot be found
texts.when: What failed, in ioFailed: the database's directory could not be found.

texts.text: the database directory cannot be created
texts.when: What failed, in ioFailed: the database's directory could not be created.

texts.text: the database file cannot be found
texts.when: What failed, in ioFailed: the database's file could not be found.

texts.text: adds members
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: Members::add.

texts.text: leaves it
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: Space::leave.

texts.text: lowers its role
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: Members::set_role on itself.

texts.text: removes members
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: Members::remove.

texts.text: sets roles
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: Members::set_role on another member.

texts.text: writes content
texts.when: What the member does, in roleRequired: a write.

texts.text: its certificate is not one
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request: the performer's certificate does not decode.

texts.text: it does not start with ncdb-erase-1:
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request: its prefix.

texts.text: it is not unpadded base64url
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: what follows its prefix is not unpadded base64url.

texts.text: it is empty
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: no layout at all.

texts.text: its length does not match its number of entries
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: the entries do not fill it.

texts.text: it names an entry twice
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: one space and person key twice.

texts.text: it is too short
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: it ends before its layout does.

texts.text: its version is not 1
texts.when: Why a text is not an erasure request or a set of sign-offs: its version byte.

texts.text: ; another context kept keys for this database meanwhile: open it again
texts.when: The hint of indexedDbRefused when IndexedDB answers ConstraintError: another tab or worker stored keys for this database meanwhile.

texts.text: IndexedDB cannot be opened
texts.when: What failed, in indexedDbRefused: IndexedDB could not be opened.

texts.text: IndexedDB cannot be read
texts.when: What failed, in indexedDbRefused: IndexedDB could not be read.

texts.text: IndexedDB cannot be used
texts.when: What failed, in indexedDbRefused: IndexedDB could not be used.

texts.text: IndexedDB cannot be written
texts.when: What failed, in indexedDbRefused: IndexedDB could not be written.

texts.text: it is not unpadded base64url
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: what follows the prefix is not unpadded base64url.

texts.text: its kind is neither a device nor an agent
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: the invitation's kind byte is neither 1 nor 2.

texts.text: its length does not match its statement byte
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: its length is not the one its statement byte gives.

texts.text: its length is not that of version 2
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: a version 2 invitation is not 66 bytes long.

texts.text: its length is not that of version 3
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: a version 3 invitation, a sub-agent's, is not 65 bytes long.

texts.text: its account key number is 0
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: its account key statement's number is 0.

texts.text: it does not start with ncdb-invite-1:
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: the text does not start with ncdb-invite-1:.

texts.text: its statement byte is neither 0 nor 1
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: its statement byte is neither 0 nor 1.

texts.text: it is too short
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: it is shorter than any version's layout.

texts.text: its version is unknown
texts.when: Why, in notAnInvitation: its version byte is one this SDK does not know.

texts.text: the key file cannot be read
texts.when: What failed, in ioFailed: the key file could not be read.

texts.text: the key file cannot be written
texts.when: What failed, in ioFailed: the key file could not be written.

texts.text: the key record cannot be sealed
texts.when: What failed, in webCryptoFailed: WebCrypto could not seal the record of the member's keys.

texts.text: access was refused
texts.when: Why, in keystoreUnreachable: the platform refused access to its keystore.

texts.text: this platform has none
texts.when: Why, in keystoreUnreachable: the platform has no keystore, as a headless Linux without the Secret Service.

texts.text: it failed
texts.when: Why, in keystoreUnreachable, for any other failure of the keystore.

texts.text: the platform failed
texts.when: Why, in keystoreUnreachable: the platform's keystore failed.

texts.text: a boolean
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: a boolean.

texts.text: a plugin's data
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: a plugin field's data.

texts.text: a float
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: a float (f64).

texts.text: an integer
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: an integer (i64).

texts.text: a list of elements
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: the elements of a set or of many links.

texts.text: an object id
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: an object id.

texts.text: a text
texts.when: What the read asked for, in fieldDoesNotHold: a text (&str).

texts.text: an admin
texts.when: The role needed, in roleRequired: an admin.

texts.text: a member
texts.when: The role needed, in roleRequired: any member.

texts.text: a writer or an admin
texts.when: The role needed, in roleRequired: a writer or an admin.

texts.text: it does not start with ncdb-sign-off-1:
texts.when: Why a text is not a set of sign-offs: its prefix.

texts.text: the wrapping key cannot be made
texts.when: What failed, in webCryptoFailed: WebCrypto could not make the non-extractable key that wraps the member's keys.

texts.text: another tab has this database open with another lock
texts.when: nc.open in a tab while another tab of the origin has the database open with another lock.

texts.text: the cursor is not of this database; start from the first page
texts.when: db.find or space.find, given a page's cursor from another database.

texts.text: the database is closed
texts.when: Any call after db.close(), and the calls still waiting when it closes.

texts.text: model.lock.json is out of date: {collection}.{field} differs from the lock in its type or options. Run ncdb model build.
texts.when: nc.open, on a model whose field has another type or other options in the lock, as when the lock was not built again after the field changed.

texts.text: model.lock.json is out of date: it has no collection {collection}. Run ncdb model build.
texts.when: nc.open, on a model that names a collection the lock does not have, as when the lock was not built again after the collection was added.

texts.text: model.lock.json is out of date: it has no field {collection}.{field}. Run ncdb model build.
texts.when: nc.open, on a model that names a field the lock does not have, as when the lock was not built again after the field was added.

texts.text: model.lock.json is out of date: it has no index {collection}.{index}. Run ncdb model build.
texts.when: nc.open, on a model that names an index the lock does not have, as when the lock was not built again after the index was added.

texts.text: model.lock.json is out of date: {collection}.{index} differs from the lock in its fields or options. Run ncdb model build.
texts.when: nc.open, on a model whose index has other fields, another equality prefix or another scope in the lock.

texts.text: the model has no such collection; pass a handle such as model.tasks
texts.when: A call given a collection that is not a handle of the model nc.open was given.

texts.text: {collection}: not a collection; declare it with nc.collection(...).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose collection is not declared with nc.collection.

texts.text: {collection}.{key}: not a computed field; declare it with nc.reach(...).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose computed field is not declared with nc.reach.

texts.text: a database name is 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, - and _
texts.when: nc.open, given a name that breaks RFC 0006's rule for a browser database's name.

texts.text: {path}: not a field; declare it with a field function such as nc.string().
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose field is not declared with a field function.

texts.text: the text is not a pairing answer: ncdb-pair-1: and unpadded base64url
texts.when: nc.pairingAnswer, given a text that does not start with ncdb-pair-1: or is not unpadded base64url.

texts.text: not a query
texts.when: A subscription to db.find or space.find, given something that is not a query.

texts.text: not a query; start one from an index, such as model.tasks.indexes.byPriority
texts.when: db.find or space.find, given something that is not a query.

texts.text: {collection}.{field} takes a safe integer, between -(2^53 - 1) and 2^53 - 1
texts.when: A write of an nc.int() field given a number that is not a safe integer.

texts.text: {collection}.{key}: not a view; declare it with nc.view(...).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose view is not declared with nc.view.

texts.text: {collection}.{key}: not an index; declare it with nc.index(...).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose index is not declared with nc.index.

texts.text: the text is not an invitation: ncdb-invite-1: and unpadded base64url
texts.when: nc.invitation, given a text that does not start with ncdb-invite-1: or is not unpadded base64url.

texts.text: the tab that held the database closed before it answered; the call may or may not have run
texts.when: A call that changes the database, sent to the tab that owned it, when that tab ended before it answered (NOC-177).

texts.text: {path}: {type} is reserved; its field type belongs to a later RFC (RFC 0005).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model with nc.richText or nc.stream, whose field types a later RFC designs.

texts.text: {path}: a set's element takes no modifiers; put them on the set.
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose nc.set element is personal, described or deprecated.

texts.text: {path}: a set's element is a basic value: nc.string(), nc.int(), nc.float(), nc.boolean() or nc.oneOf([...]).
texts.when: ncdb model build, on a model whose nc.set is of something other than a basic value.

texts.text: the worker failed: {message}
texts.when: Every call waiting on the SDK's worker when the worker fails, with the browser's own message.
